title: Cost per query and retrieval caching

videos.script: Every question a customer asks costs something, and a week of questions is a bill. {{cost}} Five hundred questions, four hundred and eighty-six model calls. Fourteen were refused before the model, and cost only their embedding. {{split}} Most of the bill is sources. A fifth of it is the same seventy-one tokens of instructions, sent with every call. {{repeat}} And most questions have been asked before. In this week's log, forty distinct ways of asking twelve things. {{exact}} An exact cache answers a repeated question without the model, if the key includes who is asking and which version of the documents answered. {{semantic}} A semantic cache goes further, matching questions by meaning. Lower its threshold a little too far, and a customer asking about cancelling a pre-order is told how to cancel an order. {{change}} When a document changes, every cached answer built on the old one has to go. {{prompt}} And prompt caching makes a long, fixed prefix cheaper to send again. {{end}} Measure first, cache what repeats, and never cache across permissions.
